newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil deputies pave way for key re-election votes.
newsitem.headline: Brazil deputies pave way for key re-election votes.

text.p: Brazil's Congress on Thursday cleared the way for a vote on whether President Fernando Henrique Cardoso can run for an unprecedented second term when they ended panel-level talks on re-election.

A congressional official said a Chamber of Deputies committee voted 18-5 to end the discussion phase of a constitutional amendment to allow re-election. Five deputies abstained. The bill was due to be put to a vote by the panel on Tuesday.
Brazil has banned re-election for holders of executive office since the republic was founded in 1889.

The vote was welcomed by government leaders who met to gauge exactly how much support they have for the controversial amendment, considered the biggest test so far of the 2-year-old Cardoso administration.
"At this point, the leaders seem very confident that they have enough votes," said a government source who was at the meeting.

If approved by the panel, the bill would probably be put to the first of two votes on the floor of the Chamber of Deputies on Wednesday, requiring a three-fifths majority, or 308 votes, on voting by both Congress and the Senate.
The source, who asked not to be identified, said leaders estimated 330 deputies were in favour of the bill.

The government's drive to approve re-election for Cardoso and for state governors and mayors, has dominated Brazilian politics for months, delaying progress on other crucial reforms to the social security and tax systems and to the civil service.

Supporters of re-election argue that an economic plan introduced by Cardoso that cut Brazil's once sky-high inflation to 10 percent in 1996, might not survive the turmoil of a change in administration.
